_comment: Real replies captured 2026-11-10 on macOS (and Linux where noted) via ROG Omni receiver (pid 1ace, interface 2). Byte indices in 'notes' include the report-ID byte at [0]. Shared test vectors for the Linux (Python) and macOS (Swift) apps.

vectors.notes: [5]=77 %, [6]=02 auto power-off step, [7]=0x14 low-battery warning 20 %, [8..9]=0x0f6d 3949 mV?, [10]=00 charging, [12]=01 unknown
charging via USB power adapter: [10]=01, [8..9]=0x101f 4127 mV (up from 3949 mV unplugged) supports the voltage hypothesis
charging via USB power adapter: [9]=01; [12..13]=00 00 while charging (voltage not reported?)

Captured 2026-11-10 on macOS, USB cable (pid 1b04, interface 1, usage page ff00). Written as 00 12 01 (65 bytes); reply has NO report ID, 64 bytes, echo starts at [0]. Indices here are relative to the echoed command: [5]=78 %, [8]=01 charging, [9]=0x14 low-battery warning 20 %, [10]=78 %, [11..12]=0x105b 4187 mV while charging (Omni reports 00 00 while charging). Omni path returned ff aa for the keyboard at the same time (keyboard asleep on the receiver).

Captured 2026-11-10 on macOS, USB cable (pid 1c0c). Vendor collection is interface 0, usage page ff01 (not interface 2 as on the Omni receiver). Written as 00 12 07 (65 bytes, accepted first try; no 64-byte fallback needed); reply has NO report ID, 64 bytes, echo starts at [0]. Indices relative to the echoed command: [4]=76 %, [5]=02 auto power-off step, [6]=0x14 low-battery warning 20 %, [7..8]=0x1047 4167 mV while charging, [9]=01 charging, [11]=01 unknown. Omni returned ff aa for the mouse at the same time.

Captured 2026-11-10 on Linux (Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0) via /dev/hidraw, ROG Omni receiver interface 2 (one hidraw node with three top-level collections ff02/ff00/ff01). Written as 03 12 07 (64 bytes); reply includes the report ID like hidapi on macOS. [5]=80 %, [7]=0x14 warning 20 %, [8..9]=0x0fa8 4008 mV?, [10]=00 not charging. Same keyboard reply as the first vector (78 %) at the same time.

Captured 2026-11-12 on Windows 11 (hidapi; each collection has its own path, Col03 = ff01 takes report ID 03). Right after the owner changed the low-battery warning from 20 % to 30 % in Armoury Crate: [7]=0x1e follows it (it was 0x14 a minute before, otherwise the same reply except [12]). So the device warning level is what Armoury Crate sets. [12] was 00 before and 01 after; earlier captures had 01, meaning unknown.

mouse_settings._comment: Real replies of the ROG Keris II Origin via the ROG Omni receiver, captured 2026-11-10 on Linux (hidraw, report ID 03). Read-only get requests; replies are zero-padded to 64 bytes. 'expect' = what squire.parse_mouse_settings must return.

captures.notes: Indices relative to the echo: [10]=00 profile 1 (0-based), [11]=04 active DPI stage (1-based), [18]=04 stages in the cycle (G-Helper), [4..6]=02 00 07 receiver firmware 07.00.02, [14..16]=09 00 01 mouse firmware 01.00.09 (same bytes as [4..6] over the cable, see mouse_settings_wired; libratbag's primary [13..15] does not fit this mouse: [12..13]=ff ff). [8]=05, [9]=07, [16]=01 unknown. Active stage confirmed on the device: from stage 4, the first DPI button press flashed red (stage 1).

[4..11]=ff: no DPI here (separate X/Y mouse, see dpi_xy). [12]=0x63: low 3 bits 3 = 1000 Hz; the high nibble 6 is not a rate (G-Helper reads it as 8000 Hz booster mode; Armoury Crate shows 1000 Hz for this mouse, owner 2026-11-12). [13]=06 unknown. [14]=02 debounce 12 ms. [16]=00 angle snapping off. [18..19]=0 angle tuning 0.
Per stage x lo/hi, y lo/hi from [4]; DPI = value * 50 + 50: 400/400, 800/800, 650/650, 3200/3200. Same values libratbag read on 2026-11-09.
RGB per stage from [4]: red, purple, black (no light), green. Confirmed on the device 2026-11-10: pressing the DPI button flashes the stage colour, cycling purple, none, green, red.
[4]=02 color cycle, [5]=0x32 brightness 50 %, [6..8] RGB (last static colour set in the libratbag test).
Zone 2 = side strip (called underglow in G-Helper and libratbag; the mouse has no light underneath).

[7]=00 low (G-Helper). [6]=ff: no surface selected (Armoury Crate captures 2026-11-12, mouse_writes.armoury_crate); [8..10] surface parameters, 00 without a surface. [5]=ff goes with no surface (00 with one).

mouse_settings_wired._comment: Real replies of the ROG Keris II Origin over the USB cable (pid 1c0c, interface 0), captured 2026-11-12 on macOS (IOKit). No report ID: the reply starts with the echo. 'expect' = what parse_mouse_settings returns with connection wired.

captures.notes: [4..6]=09 00 01 mouse firmware 01.00.09; [14..16]=00, no receiver. Profile, stage and count at the same indices as via the Omni.

mouse_writes._comment: Write commands confirmed on the ROG Keris II Origin via the ROG Omni receiver (report ID 03), 2026-11-10 on Linux. Each was approved by the owner before the first send. 'packet' = the first bytes of the 64-byte report (rest zero). Not saved (no 50 03): the change lives in the mouse's RAM. Confirmed 2026-11-10: an unsaved LED change is lost when the mouse is switched off and on; afterwards 12 03 00 reads the saved state again (colour cycle 50 %). 50 03 is needed for a change to persist.

writes.name: logo static red 100 %
writes.notes: 51 28 = set LED, [2] zone 0 = logo, [3] 00, [4] mode 00 static, [5] 0x64 = 100 %, [6..8] RGB, [9..11] direction/random/speed = 0. Confirmed by the owner: logo lit steady bright red. Read back with 12 03 00 matched.

writes.name: logo colour cycle 50 % (restore)
writes.notes: Restored the owner's setting. Read back matched.

save.notes: Save to flash. Confirmed 2026-11-10 by the owner in the settings window: logo set to static blue, Apply (write, read back, 50 03), mouse switched off and on: the logo stayed blue. Restored to colour cycle 50 % the same way.

speed_test.notes: 2026-11-10, not saved: byte [11] (G-Helper animation speed 05 fast / 09 slow) is stored per zone (read back at [12] of 12 03 NN) but has no visible effect on the Keris II Origin: colour cycle looked the same as the other zones, breathing pulsed 3 times in 10 s with 05 and with 09. Squire does not send it; restored to the owner's saved breathing 100 % #3584e4 with [11] = 00.

settings_writes._comment: Power and sensor writes confirmed on the ROG Keris II Origin via the ROG Omni receiver (report ID 03), 2026-11-12 on macOS (squire.py CLI, hidapi). Bytes from G-Helper (approved by the owner before the first send). Not saved: each was written, read back, then the original value written back. 'function' + 'args' = the squire.py builder.

writes.name: power-off 5 min, warning 30 %
writes.notes: [4] power-off code (00..04 = 1/2/3/5/10 min, ff never), [6] low-battery warning %. Read back with 12 07 [5], [6]. Restored with 51 37 00 00 02 00 14 (3 min, 20 %).

writes.name: angle snapping on
writes.notes: Field 06, value 0/1. Read back with 12 04 00 [16]. Restored with 51 31 06 00 00.

writes.name: angle tuning -10°
writes.notes: Field 0b, signed LE16 degrees (-20..20, step 5 in G-Helper). Read back with 12 04 00 [18..19]. Restored with 51 31 0b 00 00 00.

writes.name: lift-off high, surface ROG Sheath kept
writes.notes: Sent by Squire 2026-11-13 on macOS via the Omni (squire.py --set-liftoff high, unsaved), firmware 01.00.10 / receiver 07.00.08. Surface id and parameters came from the 12 06 read right before; 12 06 read back [7]=01 with the same surface. Same bytes as Armoury Crate's capture. Restored with 51 35 00 00 01 00 00 1c 34 16 (read back low, surface unchanged).

writes.name: polling 500 Hz
writes.notes: Sent by Squire 2026-11-13 on macOS via the Omni (squire.py --set-polling 500, unsaved). Index only, as Armoury Crate writes it (51 31 04 00 03 = 1000 Hz); 12 04 00 [12] read back 500 Hz in the low 3 bits. Restored with 51 31 04 00 03 (read back 1000 Hz, raw 0x63 again).

writes.name: surface Balteus Qi, lift-off kept
writes.notes: Sent by Squire 2026-11-13 on macOS via the Omni (squire.py --set-surface 0b, unsaved) from ROG Sheath; lift-off low read from 12 06 right before and kept. Same bytes as Armoury Crate. Restored with 51 35 00 00 01 00 00 1c 34 16 (ROG Sheath, read back unchanged lift-off).

armoury_crate._comment: Writes sent by Armoury Crate on Windows 11, captured with USBPcap 2026-11-12 (ROG Omni receiver, endpoint 0x03 OUT / 0x83 IN = interface 2, report ID 03). Each OUT packet was echoed unchanged on 0x83. Armoury Crate sent no reads in the capture: it writes from its own cached state. Not used by Squire yet; documentation for the next writes (not approved, see CLAUDE.md Rules).

captures.name: DPI stage 3: 650 -> 700, Apply
captures.notes: One Apply rewrites the whole sensor block, then saves. 51 31 0b = angle tuning 0 and 51 31 06 = angle snapping off (same bytes as G-Helper); 51 31 04 00 03 = polling index 3 = 1000 Hz (reads back as 0x63: the high nibble is not part of the write); 51 31 0a 00 04 = 4 stages on the DPI button; 51 31 09 00 03 = active stage, same value as 12 00 [11] (1-based: stage 3 is active afterwards, it was 4); 51 31 <stage 0-based> 00 <lo> <hi> <r g b> = DPI (v*50+50, sets X and Y alike, 12 04 02 reads 0d 00 0d 00) plus the stage colour (12 04 03). No debounce (51 31 05) and no lift-off write. Active stage 4 -> 3: the owner had to select stage 3 in Armoury Crate to edit it. Side effects the owner did not choose: angle snapping on -> off and the colour of stage 3 #000000 -> #003dff, both from Armoury Crate's own state (it overwrites values changed by other tools without reading them first). Mouse firmware 01.00.10 and receiver 07.00.08 at the time (the owner updated both in Armoury Crate the same day, from 01.00.09 / 07.00.02); all reads parse the same with the new firmware.

captures.name: lift-off low -> high (surface ROG Sheath)
captures.notes: Owner had selected the surface ROG Sheath in Armoury Crate before (not captured), then switched lift-off to high. Write (relative to 51): [2..3] 00 00, [4] surface id 01 = ROG Sheath, [5] lift-off 01 = high, [6] 00 (the echo returns 01 here: ack?), [7..9] surface parameters 1c 34 16 (from Armoury Crate's surface list, no calibration was run). Read 12 06 (relative to 12): [4] 01, [5] 00, [6] surface id, [7] lift-off, [8..10] the same parameters. On 2026-11-10 (no surface selected) 12 06 read [4] 00, [5..6] ff ff, [7] 00, [8..10] 00: surface ff = none. G-Helper writes 51 35 ff 00 ff <lift-off>, i.e. surface ff without parameters: that is why it 'resets the calibration'. A safe lift-off write keeps [6] and [8..10] from a 12 06 read.

captures.name: surface ROG Sheath -> Balteus Qi
captures.notes: Owner selected the surface Balteus Qi only: surface id 0b, parameters 1a 32 20. Armoury Crate also set lift-off back to low (00) without being asked; its UI shows low too. So a surface change in Armoury Crate resets lift-off.

captures.notes: Captured 2026-11-12, grid = row/column of the 'Preset surfaces / Mouse pad' list in Armoury Crate (9 + 9 + 3 tiles). 'Default (No calibration)' writes surface ff without parameters, the same packet as G-Helper's lift-off write (lift-off low here). Ids 02..06 and 09 do not appear. Parameters 1c 34 16 are shared by most surfaces (default tuning?). Every click wrote lift-off 00. Ended on ROG Sheath (01), lift-off low.
